name: Crescent Current Centre
description: An ivory plaza rises into two crests at the edge of Jabi Lake. The lower crest opens around the public foyer. The taller one contains the recital hall. A slim planted cut brings daylight between the two and gives the dance studio its own lakeside address.
dimensions: 82 × 54 m; two inhabited levels; 24 m crest.
arrival: A visitor ascends the broad public apron into the lake foyer, then turns inland for the recital hall. Workshops and backstage rooms have an uphill service route.
structure: A secondary steel space frame follows the two crests. Its bearings sit back from the glazed opening. Panel joints ease the curvature into repeatable strips, and a slot drain separates the plaza from the interior floor.
palette: Flamed pale granite runs from plaza to foyer. An iroko handrail returns into an indigo leather bench. Inside the recital room, narrow smoked-iroko ribs wrap the walls and acoustic canopy, with wine-red upholstered seats.
furniture: The iroko handrail turns into the back of the lake bench. A finger joint separates the straight rail from its radius. The indigo seat is removable, so it can be re-covered independently of the timber.
climate: Keep speech and music out of the gallery using a double-door sound lock. Direct intense rain away from the glazed entrance and test the drip at the shell’s lowest return.

name: Titanium Reach Museum
programme: Museum of art on the fjord
description: Three titanium lobes turn toward the water. Two limestone bars hold rectangular galleries behind them. A bridge crosses a narrow inlet and lets a visitor see the difference between the intimate galleries and the full height of the central atrium.
dimensions: 88 × 58 m; three inhabited levels; 28 m lantern.
arrival: The waterside bridge joins two gallery walks. Art handling and conservation run along the landward bar; visitors orient themselves from the atrium.
structure: A braced secondary frame carries the metal lobes independently of the rectilinear galleries. A narrow joint at the bridge lets the two gallery bars move separately. North light enters the atrium above the art-handling route.
palette: Bush-hammered pale stone, bead-blasted titanium balustrades and smoked-oak guardrails. The atrium has low felt-topped benches on black steel feet; galleries use a pale, quiet end-grain timber floor.
furniture: The felt seat floats on a folded steel foot set in from its edge. A smoked-oak hand surface lines the guard where visitors pause above the bridge; metal is left exposed on its underside.
climate: Keep meltwater out of the water-cut bridge joint. Give conservation rooms a controlled envelope and keep the most light-sensitive displays away from the atrium glazing.

name: Petal Oculus Hall
description: Nine radial bays gather around the recital chamber. Outer petals shelter people at the water courts; inner petals rise around the stage. The widened west bay opens a deliberate view of the Sabarmati and gives the hall a different front from its symmetrical precedent.
reference: Bahá’í Lotus Temple and Dubai Frame
dimensions: 56 × 56 m; main floor and balcony; 25 m apex.
arrival: Visitors cross a shallow radial water court into the circular recital chamber. A quiet perimeter gallery separates arriving audiences from backstage preparation.
structure: Radial concrete ribs rise from the annular base and support paired thin shells. Daylight enters between overlapping shells. The wider western bay frames the river before visitors turn into the music hall.
palette: Pale Makrana-type marble, warm sandstone plinths, limewashed inner ribs, teak armrests, and dark saffron wool cushions. Bronze mesh diffuses the daylight between two petals instead of covering the whole ceiling.
furniture: Teak armrests soften the edge of the stone seating plinth. Bronze mesh above the aisles filters shafts of light; dark saffron seat backs absorb light near the stage.
climate: Provide shaded waiting space before the river crossing. Keep reflecting-water filtration and acoustic isolation independent, and mock up one petal junction at full scale.

name: Estuary Spine Tower
description: White perimeter branches cradle two almond-shaped openings at the base, then narrow along the glass tower. The creek garden enters between the roots. Above, the branches pass the balconies at changing angles, becoming part of the view from the apartments.
dimensions: 44 × 36 m; 52 occupied floors at 4 m; 208 m crown.
arrival: Public arrival and deliveries separate at the podium. A fixed central core serves the residences, with a shared pool and club beneath the crown.
structure: The perimeter branches and central core share the conceptual load path. Balcony slabs terminate behind the visible Y. The inhabited garden cuts into the podium at grade without interrupting the continuous corner roots.
palette: Grey-green terrazzo with a dark stone matrix, saddle-stitched petrol-blue leather, brushed bronze reveals and fine woven palm back panels. Full-height bay glazing is set behind the white structural branches.
furniture: Petrol-blue leather is saddle-stitched onto a curved walnut frame. Woven palm forms replaceable backs in the lobby, while a terrazzo skirting separates upholstery from wet shoes.
climate: Test high-wind pressures and creek exposure before choosing the frame and glazing. Keep rain channels accessible behind balcony brows and coordinate facade-cleaning access.

name: Meridian Rift Tower
description: Two glazed halves turn past one another above a shared plaza. The diagonal rift remains visible all the way to the crown. Three bridges cross it at different heights so the building’s most unusual space is also part of the working day.
dimensions: 54 × 40 m; 44 occupied floors at 4 m; 176 m crest.
arrival: The plaza continues into a full-height atrium. Two independent vertical cores work on opposite sides. Enclosed bridges connect the halves at three defined levels.
structure: Two independent cores reach ground on opposite sides of the atrium. Curved floor edges are carried back to each core. Bridges at L12, L24 and L36 bridge the fissure and can accommodate relative movement.
palette: Blackened aluminium balcony noses, brushed bronze rails, smoke-coloured terrazzo and celadon wool. An oval reception desk is clad in vertically brushed pewter. The atrium floor and balcony edges reflect more softly than a mirror.
furniture: A pewter desk has vertical brush marks that conceal small scratches. Celadon bridge seats sit low enough to keep the changing section visible from both directions.
climate: Study wind and stack effect, fire compartments and smoke extraction through the tall atrium. Separate bridge movement from glazed enclosure tolerances.

name: Tidefold Tower
description: The waterfront podium turns into four rounded glass lobes. The twist eases as the tower rises; one deeply recessed sky garden marks the upper floors. A transparent crown puts the ballroom, rather than plant or signage, at the top of the public silhouette.
dimensions: 50 × 42 m; 50 occupied floors at 4 m; 200 m crest.
arrival: The street lobby joins the waterfront promenade. Upper offices surround a fixed core. A planted terrace occupies L27 and the ballroom occupies the crown.
structure: The cores remain fixed as perimeter plates turn near the base. Four broad glass lobes settle into a clear crown. A recessed L27 terrace opens one side while keeping the continuous service route above.
palette: Pale celadon glass, satin nickel, cream limestone and fluted cast-glass screens. Dark mulberry upholstery on crescent benches makes the rounded lobby legible; the crown ballroom has a finely ribbed ash floor.
furniture: A mulberry crescent seat makes the lobby’s curved glass legible at body height. The ballroom floor changes direction across the lobe with thin ash strips and quiet movement joints.
climate: Coordinate wind loading, sun control and access around the bulging corners. Simulate driven rain at the garden notch and protect terrace doors with a drained threshold.

name: Cala Shell Residence
description: The roof wraps a private pool court in a single almond-shaped contour. Its upper lip lifts to give the salon shade and an open sea view. The landward shell thickens into the entry cleft and protects the upper bedrooms from the arrival path.
dimensions: 38 × 23 m; two levels; 8 m shell crest.
arrival: An uphill cleft leads into the upper sleeping wing; a stair curls down to the sheltered salon and pool terrace. A service passage follows the thick landward flank.
structure: A curved perimeter beam follows the almond shell and supports its tapering cantilever over the water. Glazing stays back from the sharp lip. The uphill entry breaks the contour without closing the sea view.
palette: Pearl-toned exterior, pale bush-hammered limestone on the terrace, waxed walnut inside and sea-green linen. A curved walnut banquette sits at the sheltered end of the pool court; its cushion seams follow the aperture.
furniture: The curved walnut banquette is built in segments; cushion seams stop at the panel joints. A pale stone curb distinguishes the pool from the living floor even when both surfaces are wet.
climate: Shield the long glazed salon from low summer sun. Separate pool-water drainage from roof runoff and use a replaceable marine-facing edge trim.

name: Treecrown Residence
description: The family occupies a low glazed wing embedded in the forest floor. Two inclined concrete stems carry a pair of glazed capsules above the trees. One capsule holds the bedroom, the other a reading room. The lift slit between the stems makes the ascent visible from outside.
dimensions: 38 × 24 m base; two low levels and a crown floor at +18 m; 22 m crest.
arrival: The low family wing sits against the slope. A lift and enclosed stair within the mast serve a high, private sleeping and reading floor.
structure: Two inclined concrete stems transfer the sleeping capsules back to the embedded base. The mast encloses lift and stair; its narrow slot exposes the ascent. The lower roof steps into the forest floor.
palette: Ivory mineral concrete, blackened elm casework, brushed pewter pulls and moss-green wool. Shoji-like vertical screens sit inside insulated glass; the crown has a fixed elm bed ledge and a single paper reading lamp.
furniture: A blackened-elm bed ledge follows the crown window. An independent interior screen can close for privacy without changing the silhouette of the glazed capsule.
climate: Test crown vibration, snow loading, seismic response and foundations on the sloping site. Keep forest drainage outside the lower retaining walls.

name: Strata Prow Villa
place: Hout Bay, Cape Town, South Africa
description: A thin roof projects above a thicker triangular terrace. Between them, a long pool narrows toward the prow, and the living rooms open along the sheltered side. Only the inland windbreak curves; the roof and pool keep their sharp edges.
dimensions: 42 × 26 m; two levels; 9 m roof edge.
arrival: The upper entry opens onto the short end of the wedge. Living and dining share its long sea edge; bedrooms sit below, with a protected service route on the uphill side.
structure: The projecting roof plane is back-spanned into the uphill service wall. The long pool occupies the thicker lower terrace; a separate drainage zone protects the living-room sill from splash and sea spray.
palette: Shell-white fair-faced concrete, honed charcoal quartzite, weathered bronze and oxblood saddle leather. A tapered walnut dining table meets the pool-facing wall with a concealed expansion joint.
furniture: A tapered walnut dining table echoes the prow in plan. Its hidden expansion joint permits seasonal movement while a straight sightline remains open to the headland.
climate: Model wind suction at the thin tip. Inspect waterproofing and provide a repair route along the more sheltered landward edge of the pool.

name: Split Ribbon Duplex
description: A continuous white ribbon rises over two independent front doors, dips at the party wall and lifts again over the second home. From the garden, two separate patios make that division equally clear. Each household has two upstairs bedrooms and its own stair.
reference: Heydar Aliyev Center and Shell Villa
arrival: Each home has its own street door, stair, kitchen, two upper bedrooms and private rear garden. The shared dip in the roof marks the party line from the street.
structure: Independent dwelling frames meet at a continuous party wall. The white ribbon dips above that wall, then rises over two separate glazed fronts. A split gutter follows the low point so the two homes have independent rainwater services.
palette: Brass gauze, iroko ceiling battens and indigo strip-woven aso-oke upholstery. Honey-toned terrazzo floors wrap the stairs. One walnut settle fits each ribbon's concave wall; each home has its own garden.
furniture: Indigo strip-woven panels run across a removable settle back. Each textile width is visible at its stitched seam; iroko battens continue the ceiling rhythm through the shaded rear patio.
climate: Provide acoustic and fire separation at the full party-wall height. The deep brow shades glazing and keeps the private garden thresholds sheltered in heavy rain.

name: Twin Prow Duplex
description: Two white terrace planes point in opposite directions on the Atlantic slope. The lower home reaches its garden on one level. A stone blade conceals the separate stair to the upper maisonette, keeping the two arrivals private.
dimensions: 22 × 16 m; garden flat plus two-storey maisonette; 11 m crest.
arrival: The street splits into two entrances. One reaches the garden flat directly. The second climbs behind a stone blade to the upper two-level dwelling.
structure: Two straight terrace planes project in opposite directions. A stone blade conceals the stair to the upper maisonette, separating its entrance from the garden flat. Each roof fall drains to its own service edge.
palette: Oxide-red lime plaster, smoked chestnut, sea-green glazed ceramic at wash points and rope-webbed dining chairs. Recessed tracks let curtains stack inside the taper rather than obstruct the glass.
furniture: A rope-webbed dining chair keeps air moving through the seat. Curtain stacks disappear behind smoked chestnut reveals so the wedge-shaped opening stays clear when the glass opens.
climate: Check wind pressure at the Atlantic-facing prows. Keep the public entry stair independent of the lower private garden and provide a non-slip sheltered landing.

name: Lagoon Arc Hotel
place: Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
description: Two occupied flanks rise into an upper bridge. The empty oval between them frames the open Gulf from the entrance. A champagne-coloured screen with palm-vein perforations gives shade to the guestrooms while preserving the continuous ring.
reference: Museum of the Future and Dubai Frame
dimensions: 80 × 52 m; five principal levels; 28 m crest.
arrival: One side of the oval contains guestrooms; the opposite side holds dining and shared lounges. The upper bridge joins them over the sea-facing opening. Service circulation follows the landward spine.
structure: Two thick occupied flanks carry a high bridge above the sea portal. Floors continue around the opening while the champagne skin makes the overall loop legible from the beach. The date-palm perforation is a separate outer screen.
palette: Brushed champagne metal, warm limestone, date-palm woven panels, ink-green mohair and travertine with small open pits. A radial lobby settee follows the portal; guest beds use woven headboards with bronze pins.
furniture: A radial settee changes from limestone base to ink-green mohair at hand height. Palm-frond panels are fixed to removable frames; bronze pins repeat at a consistent spacing on the guest headboards.
climate: Study salt, wind and reflected glare; separate beach-level routes from service access. Test the upper bridge movement and the shading of guestrooms along the curve.

name: River Confluence Hotel
description: Two unequal towers share a three-level waterfront podium. The podium’s diamond panels open gradually into the tower glazing. At ground level a split river stair brings guests to the shared lobby, where each wing has its own lift bank.
dimensions: 66 × 46 m podium; river wing 18 floors / 72 m; city wing 26 floors / 104 m.
arrival: The river stair leads into a shared lobby. Each accommodation wing has its own lift bank. Service kitchens and laundry enter through the city side of the podium.
structure: The three-level podium gathers both hotel cores and a public waterfront stair. Diamond fibre-concrete panels open progressively into glazing at the two tower bases. The taller city wing continues above the river wing.
palette: Silver-grey diamond GFRC, dark grey limestone, stitched pandan-weave panels and oxblood lacquer. Over the lobby bar a pale ribbed metal canopy narrows like the podium's glazed throat; bedrooms use ventilated woven panels and oval reading lamps.
furniture: Pandan-weave wall panels sit in removable cassettes behind the oxblood reception seating. The faceted canopy over the bar borrows the podium joint spacing at a smaller scale.
climate: Test wind-driven rain at the glazed throat. Keep receiving and linen routes on the city edge, and separate the two guest lift groups through the public base.

name: Stream Ledge House
place: Hudson Valley near Woodstock, New York, USA
description: A fieldstone chimney anchors two concrete terrace trays above the rocky stream. An entry bridge reaches the stone spine from uphill. The upper writing room looks back through the canopy, while the lower salon follows the water horizontally.
dimensions: 24 × 17 m; two floors; 8 m upper parapet.
arrival: A footbridge reaches the stone spine. The living area turns toward the stream, with two quiet rooms upstairs and a writing ledge over the lower terrace.
structure: Stone masonry encloses the core while cantilevered terrace slabs step toward the water. The writing ledge sits above a shorter lower tray. The hearth boulder sets the living-room floor datum.
palette: Flagstone floors bend around a hearth boulder. Cherry built-ins follow the slab edges, lichen-green wool covers a window seat, and a shallow aged-copper hearth hood catches reflected water light.
furniture: Waxed cherry shelves terminate against the stone with a narrow movement gap. Lichen wool softens the stream-facing window seat while a copper hood reflects light back into the hearth.
climate: Confirm flood levels and ecological limits before siting the bridge. Check cantilever deflection, freeze-thaw durability and water shedding at every terrace return.

name: Dune Veil House
description: A white shell rises from one side of the dune and lifts along the sea-facing veranda. An off-centre oculus brings a protected garden into the plan. Living spaces line the long glazed lip; bedrooms open from the sheltered landward hall.
reference: Heydar Aliyev Center and Shell Villa
dimensions: 22 × 15 m; one occupied level; 5.5 m roof crest.
arrival: A sheltered arrival court separates the bedroom wing from the sea-facing living room. The kitchen and utility open to a service yard on the landward side.
structure: The roof lands on one side and lifts to shelter the seaward veranda. A thickened ring around the planted oculus stabilises the opening. Surface water exits through the landward service yard.
palette: Cork-faced storage doors, pale sanded ash, sea-green lacquer and slung natural linen. The fixed daybed fits the long crescent window; small bronze pulls are recessed into the cork. Lime floors are softly burnished.
furniture: Cork cabinet doors have recessed bronze pulls; a ventilated plinth holds them above the floor. A fixed ash daybed follows the crescent window, leaving the planted court as the room’s centre.
climate: Monitor sand drift and salt exposure at the low edge. Size the court drain and overflow independently and keep both reachable from the garden path.
